subject: Harborline - Elevated error rate & throughput degradation: post-incident follow-through
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@harborline.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harborline SRE Team <sre@harborline.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors & slowdowns impacting embed pipeline

Hi Stephanie —

We saw a sharp uptick in 500s and tail latency on our embedding calls starting ~15:45 PT today. Throughput dropped ~40% for ~25 minutes; retries from our side increased which pushed token cost up and impacted our downstream matching jobs.

This affected a handful of critical nightly jobs and our CX team escalated. Can you confirm whether this was an outage on Redwood or a routing/region issue on our side? We need an exec readout and a timeline + corrective actions.

Rajiv
Senior Engineering Manager, Harborline

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@harborline.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors & slowdowns impacting embed pipeline

Rajiv —

Thanks for flagging and sorry for the disruption. We started an incident bridge immediately when alerts fired. Quick summary from our on-call: a hotshard imbalance in the autoscaler combined with a short-lived kernel preemption on the instance serving the long-tail requests resulted in increased queuing and elevated 500s for ~23 minutes.

Actions we took within the window:
- Rerouted new requests to healthy pools and bumped capacity for Harborline's tenant pool.
- Kicked the KV cache warmers for active prefixes to reduce cold-start tail latency.
- Rolled a micro-fix for the autoscaler scoring to avoid the imbalance recurring.

We're compiling a full timeline and a post-incident write-up with recommended follow-through. I'll share by EOD Monday with exec-level summary + action owner assignments.

Stephanie
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: logs and quick triage notes (Harborline)

Folks —

Attached are preliminary captures from the affected GPU host and the autoscaler event trace (see support_logs_20270409.zip). Early notes: the preemption correlated with a kernel OOM signal on host g10-7; while the host recovered quickly, the autoscaler’s scoring function treated the degraded host as healthy for ~90s, which delayed full traffic draining. That window is likely responsible for the 500 spikes.

Proposed immediate mitigations for Monday:
1) Make the autoscaler treat kernel-level preemption flags as a hard signal and trigger instant drain. (owner: Marcus)
2) Add a short-circuit to our request router to bypass nodes with recent kernel preemptions for 5m. (owner: Aditya)
3) Create an SLO-backed warm-up for Harborline’s busiest prefixes to reduce cold-start token churn. (owner: Grace)

I started a draft RCA doc and timeline — will fold in customer notes before send.

Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@harborline.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@harborline.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Harborline incident 2027-04-09 — post-incident summary and next steps

Rajiv / Karen —

Please find attached our post-incident summary (harborline_rca_20270411.pdf) and an event timeline (harborline_incident_timeline_20270409.csv). Executive summary below:

Executive summary:
- Impact window: 2027-04-09 15:45:20–16:08:50 PT.
- Customer-facing effect: ~40% throughput reduction and ~6–8% 500 responses for high-concurrency embed requests; downstream batch jobs were delayed.
- Root cause: a GPU host experienced a kernel-level preemption (OOM-related) while the autoscaler misclassified the host state, delaying traffic draining and causing a cascading request queue buildup.

Corrective actions & owners (target dates):
- Autoscaler hard-fail on kernel preemption flags (Marcus) — target: 2027-04-14
- Router short-circuit around recently preempted nodes (Aditya) — target: 2027-04-15
- Tenant-level SLO warm-up (Grace) — pilot for Harborline prefixes by 2027-04-21
- Billing credit proposal and cost reconciliation for retry inflation (Stephanie) — proposal by 2027-04-13

We will update this thread as each item progresses and share a runbook for the warm-up pilot. If you want a 30-minute executive readout, we can schedule for Wednesday; otherwise we’ll follow up with the status updates and the credit note.

Thanks again for your patience — we take this seriously and want to ensure it doesn’t recur.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: harborline_rca_20270411.pdf (post-incident write-up), harborline_incident_timeline_20270409.csv (event timeline)

Subject: Re: Harborline incident 2027-04-09 — post-incident summary and next steps

Stephanie —

Appreciate the quick, clear summary and the ownership. Two asks from our side before we sign off:
1) Can you share the expected exposure window for other tenants when autoscaler changes are rolled? We need assurance this fix won't unintentionally increase tail latency for our other pipelines.
2) Please include a proposed credit amount (est. token cost delta) in the credit proposal.

We'd prefer a short exec readout on Wed to sign off on the credit and the pilot cadence. 30 minutes at 10:00 PT works for Rajiv and me.

Karen
Director of Platform Engineering, Harborline

Subject: Re: Harborline incident 2027-04-09 — post-incident summary and next steps

Karen / Rajiv —

Thanks — 10:00 PT Wednesday confirmed for exec readout (calendar invite sent). Quick answers inline:
1) Autoscaler rollout exposure: Marcus and I validated a canary strategy that restricts the immediate behavior change to 5% of clusters with a traffic-slice that excludes Harborline tenants during the initial 24h. We'll publish the rollout plan in the shared Drive link.
2) Credit estimate: preliminary estimate attached in the RCA doc (section 4) — roughly $1,950 in incremental token/retry spend for the impacted window; final reconciliation after billing run (owner: Stephanie) by 2027-04-13.

Action items updated in the Drive doc; we'll track deliverables in SUP-6123. Looking forward to the readout.

Best,
Stephanie
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
